agree.reason: The memo's open concession on the renovation and its plain handling of the budget would earn this skeptical GM's trust, but it never shows why the writer beats an outside candidate who ran a bigger desk, so he may still lean outside.

honest.reason: The memo rightly refuses to claim the writer was the main cause of the score rise, but it overreaches in calling hiring and training 'the two biggest drivers of front desk payroll' and in saying an outside hire would learn 'from scratch.'

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the raw figures without working them: it never states turnover as 64% falling to 36%, and it never combines the two changes into total training shifts (about 81 down to about 25), which would also have backed up the payroll point.

right_comparison.reason: The memo describes the outside alternative as someone starting from scratch while the job stays open, but the GM is already interviewing an experienced front desk manager from a larger hotel, so that picture doesn't match the facts.

qualification.reason: The six-month plan of monthly reviews against budget gives the GM something to check and a time frame, but it sets no variance threshold and says nothing about what happens if payroll goes off track.

objections.reason: It answers the renovation objection well by pointing out that check-in is the part of the stay the front desk delivers, and it raises the budget gap honestly, but it never takes on the outside candidate's bigger-hotel experience.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo with clear headings and a direct request, which matches the brief.
